Random forest. Okay. Now, there is one more thing which we call random search CV. Actually, it is called randomized search CV. So, what happens in this is that here you have 108 combinations. Right. Now, if this is a very big data set or if you have to train more hyper parameters, then grid search CV becomes a little slow and you take a lot of time to train the model. What does randomized search CV do? That it randomly, if you have 108 options, then randomly,

will select 10, 15, 20 and will perform everything randomly. So, what I did here? I added one or two additional parameters like Bootstrap, MinSampleSplit, MinSampleLeaf. I used more hyperparameters. This is my parameter grid. It is a little bigger this time. Then I called RandomizeSearchCV. Here I kept everything the same as it is. And when I trained this, you can see

fitting 5 folds for 10 candidates. In short, it randomly picked up 10 candidates and left the rest. So this process is much faster. Although you don't get the best results in this, but you get the answer quickly. So in short, if you are working on a very big data set, as you can see here, your answer is only 0.81. Clearly, there are better answers hidden, but we can't get them out because in randomized search, you select randomly.

Okay? So, it is possible that you may not get the best answers. So, you must be having a question in your mind. Then, why will I use randomized search CV? Answer is, whenever you are working on a very big dataset and you have to tune a lot of hyperparameters, in that case, you will use randomized search CV. Why? Because it can give you good results by selecting randomly. If you use grid search CV on a very big dataset, then you can get such a good result. I mean, you will get a good result.

If you give enough time, you will get a good result. But it will take a lot of time. I mean a lot. Depending on the data set. So in short, in summary, you have to use grid search CV when you have less data and the algorithm you are using has less hyperparameters. But if you have a very big data set and the algorithm you have has a lot of hyperparameters, then you should use randomized search CV. It gives you near to perfect result in less time.
